content.text:
I found nothing in the document that the record contradicts or fails to support, so I made no flags.

- **Cause claims:** The root cause, the plain-words cause and causal chain 3 all rest on F1, Code-Fix's reading of the source that nothing ran. Each one is hedged ("likely", "unverified"), so they pass.
- **"Too few replicas" (causal chain 2):** This line is stated as fact, so it was the closest call. I accepted it because the record shows the floor raised from 3 to 6 replicas (M1, T22), the rule that fired then stopped firing, and the action was judged confirmed (T20–T21). Flag it if you'd want that line hedged too.
- **What-if sentences:** The two "had it been otherwise" sentences describe what would have happened, so I didn't judge them.
- **Action items:** These propose rather than claim, so I didn't judge them either.

supported.quote: The production autoscaler settings for io-shop set the scale-down stabilization window to {F1.3}, so the controller acts on the lower CPU per replica that its own scale-up to {F1.5} replicas produced, drops straight back to {F1.6}, and at that count CPU per replica climbs past its {F1.7} target and requests queue, which drives response times up until it scales up again. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
The shop's automatic scaling likely kept taking away the extra servers it had just added, which left too few servers to answer shoppers quickly.
io-shop's pages could slow down again in the same way if its autoscaler floor goes back to {T22.2} replicas while the scale-down setting in its repository is still unchanged.
Shop pages slowed down for shoppers
Shoppers had to wait much longer than usual for io-shop's slowest requests to finish, while the share of failed requests stayed within its normal variation.
rows: Rise above baseline: none beyond its normal variation

supported.quote: io-shop had too few replicas serving it for the load it was under.
When the Investigator read the rollout at {T10.1}, all {T10.2} replicas were running a single revision.
The autoscaler likely dropped back to its floor of {F1.6} replicas right after each scale-up, since the production values file sets its scale-down stabilization window to {F1.3}.
No check was seen that would stop an autoscaler setting with a zero scale-down stabilization window from reaching production.
No alert on the autoscaler moving io-shop's replica count back and forth was seen.
The fault was found only by the latency alert.
Nobody was paged: the alert was not linked to any on-call incident.
rows: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.
